status: pre-registered test of the wirkungskette_v01 review classes on unseen Hangmuren areas; written before any score is computed in these areas
question: Do the review classes of the frozen V0.4 static model place documented, precisely located pure Hangmuren of unseen event documentations into the top 5 % / 20 % of the assessable area more often than slope alone and than the area share?
requested_by: user via the website session, 2026-10-18 ('Den Demo-Test würde ich machen, wie du empfohlen hast. Aber ich würde sagen, zuerst einmal mit Gebiet rechnen.'), design from PROJEKTBEWERTUNG_VOR_ZUSAMMENFUEHRUNG.md sections 5 and 6

inventory.source: data/raw/geosphere_natural_hazards.json (GeoSphere Austria Naturgefahren inventory, local copy, read only)
inventory.campaign_year_rule: the single four-digit year contained in RegKatE_ID
inventory.target_process: Prozessuntergruppe (stripped) == 'Hangmure' (pure Hangmuren only; mixed classes are not targets)

areas.campaign_rule: every campaign with 2000 <= campaign year <= 2015 and >= 50 precisely located pure Hangmuren
areas.unseen_reason: the V0.4 model was trained only on events from 2016 onwards; campaigns before 2016 were never used for training, selection or evaluation
areas.boundary_source: Eurostat GISCO LAU 2021, 1:1 million (https://gisco-services.ec.europa.eu/distribution/v2/lau/geojson/LAU_RG_01M_2021_4326.geojson), Austrian units only (CNTR_CODE == 'AT')
areas.boundary_rule: area of a campaign = union of the LAU 2021 municipalities that contain >= 5 of the campaign's precisely located pure Hangmuren (point in polygon)
areas.boundary_limitation: municipalities are chosen because events lie in them, and the true survey extent of each documentation is unknown; slopes inside that were not surveyed count as background. Boundaries are official and drawn independently of the point pattern inside them. 1:1 million generalisation shifts edges by up to a few hundred metres
areas.targets: the campaign's precisely located pure Hangmuren inside its area; events outside are counted and reported, never used
areas.windows: one terrain window per connected component of the area (bbox + catchment margin); cells are 90 m grid cells whose centre lies in the area and inside Austria

terrain.primary_dem: SRTM 1 arc-second (SRTMGL1 v3, acquisition 11-22 February 2000), ESA STEP mirror https://step.esa.int/auxdata/dem/SRTMGL1/<tile>.SRTMGL1.hgt.zip, no login
terrain.date_rule: provenance of the height data must precede the campaign year (user decision 2026-10-18: provenance counts instead of the file date)
terrain.date_rule_consequence: Tilezen/Mapzen documentation lists the 10 m data.gv.at DGM (airborne laser scanning of the federal states) as the Austrian source of the Skadi tiles; its acquisitions are not demonstrably before 2005-2015, so Skadi does not satisfy the provenance rule here. SRTM (February 2000) does for every area.
terrain.known_shift: the V0.4 model was trained on Skadi (laser-scan based) features; SRTM is a C-band radar surface model including vegetation and buildings and is smoother. The model is applied unchanged; slope is computed on the same SRTM grid, so model and baseline share the shift
terrain.secondary_dem: Skadi (same tiles as V0.4) as a labelled sensitivity analysis only: provenance not demonstrably pre-event

land_cover.rule: latest CORINE vintage whose imagery ended before the campaign year: CLC2000 (imagery 1999-2001) for 2002-2007, CLC2006 (2005-2007) for 2008-2012, CLC2012 (2011-2012) for 2013-2018
land_cover.classes_from: config/v04.json features.land_cover.classes (unchanged mapping of CORINE codes to the five model classes)
land_cover.missing: no or several polygons covering a point = not assessable (V0.4 rule)

geology: GeoSphere Austria 1:500 000, five V0.4 classes (static map, unchanged)

model.use: linear score of the frozen V0.4 static conditional logit, applied unchanged; no refit, no tuning

baseline: slope alone (higher slope = higher rank), same cells, same SRTM grid

metric.classes: per area, cutoffs from the scores of all assessable grid cells: top 5 % and top 20 %
metric.capture: a target event is captured at k % if its own 30 m cell is assessable and its score reaches the area's top-k % cutoff; non-assessable target events count as not captured for both methods
metric.primary: capture at 20 %, mean over areas with equal area weights
secondary: share of target events not assessable
metric.primary_comparison: paired difference model minus slope in the primary metric

uncertainty.units: areas (one campaign = one storm episode). Vorarlberg/Tirol and Gasen/Haslau August 2005 may belong to the same synoptic event; reported, not merged
uncertainty.method: two-stage cluster bootstrap: resample areas with replacement, then within each drawn area resample 2 km x 2 km blocks (EPSG:31287 grid) of target events with replacement; cutoffs from grid cells stay fixed
uncertainty.claim_rule: 'better than slope' only if the 95 % interval of the paired difference excludes 0; 'better than chance' only if the interval of the capture share lies above the chance reference; otherwise 'no established benefit'

spatial_overlap_report: number of V0.4 training (development) events lying inside each area is reported; no exclusion
procedure: pilot on one area (smallest by target count) to check the technical chain
freeze results (write-once) before building the demo
demo_rule: after the test is frozen: demo area = campaign with the most precisely located pure Hangmuren; demo centre = representative point of its municipality with the most of them
after_test: the user plans to use all inventory data (including 2005 and earlier) for a new training model; from then on the tested areas are seen data
